newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds steady, little impact seen from output data.
newsitem.headline: Bunds steady, little impact seen from output data.

text.p: German Bunds were moderately firmer in early trade on Monday, buoyed by Friday's gains in U.S. Treasuries.
Dealers said Bunds were unlikely to move much during the session as trading was subdued by the the UK May Day holiday.
German data due on Monday and Tuesday are expected to confirm the trend of modest economic growth and are therefore unlikely to elicit a major market response, dealers said.
Bunds were quoted up 12 basis points at 101.72 at 0744 GMT after moving in a range of 101.71 to 101.88 so far this session.
German industrial production for March, due at 0830 GMT today, is expected to show a 0.3 percent rise month-on-month and a 4.6 percent increase year-on-year, according to a Reuter poll of economists.
April jobless data, expected to be released on Tuesday, are expected to show a slight drop due mainly to the improving weather.
"Both factors indicate that the upswing is still faltering," HPO-Research said in a market commentary. The data should underpin a sideways movement in Bunds, the bank added.
One Frankfurt-based dealer said Tuesday's jobless data was unlikely to be supportive for Bunds but added that he did not expect the figures to have much impact.
"German data usually don't have that much of an effect on the market," he said, adding that U.S. data frequently have more impact on Bunds.
The next U.S. figures due are March housing completions, scheduled to be released at 1230 GMT, followed on Tuesday by March factory orders.
